footer.credit: The prototype, its photos and schematics — Mohit Bhoite, bhoite.com/sculptures/lander-r2. Lander R2 is an unofficial demo project inspired by it.
hero.intro: With Claude Code anyone can add their own widget to a device like this in an evening. Our goal is not another gadget but a widget platform and a community around it, the Flipper and Pebble way.
idea.title: Why a platform, not a gadget
idea.lead: Flipper and Pebble didn't win on hardware. They let people write their own app in an evening and publish it. Here the bar is even lower.
idea.p1: A Lander R2 widget is one function: “draw a screen from this data”. Claude Code writes it in five minutes from a plain-language description: “show my next meeting and blink blue five minutes before it”.
idea.p2: The device is the excuse. The product is a widget catalog, event scenarios and a community that trades them. Below is an interactive demo: pick screens and run scenarios to see how the device reacts.
idea.v1: One file, one draw(data) function. No SDK, no builds — Claude Code writes and verifies it.
idea.v2: Meeting in 5 min, CI failed, Claude asked a question — the device reacts with the screen, LED and sound.
idea.v3: AMOLED with touch for interaction and animation; e-ink for weeks of battery. One body, one widget catalog.
idea.v4: Widgets and scenarios live in the GitHub repo. Propose yours via an issue.

src.note: Official pages: Waveshare Wiki (Display/Touch Control tables and header pinout — from a saved copy of the docs), Adafruit Learn, Espressif's arduino-esp32 repository, ST, Bosch, Vishay, Analog Devices. “Verified” — GPIO numbers taken directly from the vendor's documentation; the rest comes from prior experience and must be checked before soldering.
fw.title: Firmware
fw.lead: Description only — no firmware code on this page.
fw.p1: The screen is drawn with Adafruit GFX + Adafruit ST7735/ST7789. The background is a static 170×320 BMP read from the display board’s SD card; only changing data is drawn on top.
fw.p2: Weather and moon phase reach the Photon 2 through Particle Webhooks: the Particle cloud calls OpenWeather and a moon API and returns a short response that a simple parser picks apart.
fw.p3: Original code and the author’s other projects are on GitHub: github.com/mohitbhoite
